NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

Just before Wall Street opened up for trading, Rene Hass, who formerly ran Nvidia’s datacenter business long before the GenAI boom exploded on the scene and who was reportedly the top contender to take on the chief executive officer of Nvidia, announced that he had extended his contract as CEO of chip designer and now chip maker Arm Holdings out to 2033. About a half hour later, Nvidia put out an 8-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that reinstated Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer, and board member, roles that he resigned from – but importantly was not fired from – back on November 12 after several scandals came to light. The 8-K was sparsely worded: “On November 22, 2026, the board of directors of Nvidia Corporation reinstated Jen-Hsun Huang as Nvidia’s president, chief executive officer and member of the board of directors, effective immediately. Following the reinstatement of Mr. Huang, Ms. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer.” A few minutes later, Nvidia’s investor relations organization put out a more detailed statement, which reversed the statement that chairman of the board Harvey Jones, which has been a board member of Nvidia since soon after it was founded in April 1993, made in his new role as chairman, saying at the beginning of the call to go over Nvidia’s third quarter of fiscal 2027 financial results on November 18 that the “Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and was engaged in an executive search to find a new CEO to run the company. cards.body: Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries. The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk." President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard." Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang. Shares of Nvidia closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6. "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process." With that off the table, then there was the challenge of alleged workplace conduct. Workplace conduct is always a challenge because it opens NVIDIA up to claims from current and former employees. There was an early 2010’s case in California (note I have a 2007 JD from California’s largest law school, but never practiced, so this is not legal advice) for workplace sexual harassment in the $168M range, that was then significantly reduced to under $100M, then settled. What I have been telling folks for the past week and a half is that for the company to lose $1T in shareholder value, even $1B in a legal fund pays a lot of attorneys to cover other claims. It felt like Jensen’s value was wildly out of line with what it would cost to settle the cases. The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Clayton said the investigation was "ongoing" on Sunday, the day before Nvidia announced it had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a position he resigned from in part because of his relationship with Alice Huang. Alice Huang was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia. U.S. intelligence reportedly believes she is a Chinese spy. "There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel. They are the absolute top that everybody wants, that's why we're focusing on this." Nvidia's board announced Jensen Huang's return before the opening bell on Monday, saying it had "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. It added that it received input from senior levels of the United States government" and is confident that his reinstatement "poses no national security risk." Last week, the Commerce and Justice departments said that the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 over potential export-control violations. Their joint statement said Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security and Singapore law enforcement interviewed Huang during an on-site check in June 2025. The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation. cards.body: Original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) supplying servers to AI data centers are reportedly raising prices by as much as 45 percent, months after contracts have been signed. The FT reports that the likes of Dell, Lenovo, Supermicro, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) are demanding far higher prices from customers when equipment is ready to be delivered than the initially contracted figures. The report suggests price hikes have started to hit some of the biggest equipment buyers beyond hyperscale customers, such as financial trading firms building out IT infrastructure. OEMs passing on skyrocketing costs from the ongoing memory shortage to customers is the likely cause. The shortage has already caused price increases in the enterprise networking space, hitting segments like fixed-wireless access equipment and campus Ethernet switches. And the dearth shows no signs of slowing, with SK Hynix upping its previous projection for relief from 2028 to 2030. Suppliers have sought to alleviate some of the pain, with HPE promising to guarantee price quotes on compute, storage, and infrastructure below $1 million, as well as doubling its pricing quote validity period from 15 days to 30 days. Cisco also upped its compute price protection and price quote validity for servers to 14 days back in August. But such niceties are few and far between. Per FT sources, GPU server prices have risen by at least 20 to 30 percent of late, while CPU nodes have tripled. Memory hardware prices have also skyrocketed. TrendForce suggests contract prices for server dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) in the second half of 2025 alone jumped 64 percent – a number that could rise as high as 270 percent by the end of this year. The research firm also warned that high-bandwidth memory, vital for GPUs, could even rise by 70–140 percent in 2027. As a result, engineers are having to get innovative with the hardware they already have. For example, Nvidia’s scale-in networking concept offloads heavier security and storage tasks from the main server processor to boost compute performance, while optimizing the Key-Value (KV) cache could help reduce footprints and prevent wasted capacity. AMD, meanwhile, is banking on software playing a part in easing costs. Solutions from the recently acquired Mext trick operating systems into making flash storage function as high-speed DRAM. By predicting memory demand, it swaps less-used memory pages between DRAM and non-volatile memory express (NVMe) flash, providing users with the same performance but on a memory option that is 50 times cheaper per bit and requires 30 times less power per bit.

related.title: U.S. adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist over export control concerns amid Nvidia controversy

cards.body: The U.S. has added Singapore-based Megaspeed and six other Southeast Asian companies to its trade blacklist, citing national security and foreign policy concerns. The Department of Commerce in a Federal Register filing cited a "significant risk" of companies being or becoming involved in diverting advanced computing products to unauthorized end users or end uses. The blacklisting comes as Jensen Huang returns to the helm of Nvidia following his departure amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is under investigation by U.S. authorities. Megaspeed International is a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia. The restrictions apply to all items subject to U.S. Export Administration Regulations, with license applications to be reviewed under a "presumption of denial." The blacklist also includes PT Megaspeed International and MSFusion Sdn. Bhd. in Malaysia, as well as Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd. The filing identified 7Road International as an alias used by both Megaspeed's Singapore and Thailand entities. The Commerce Department initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations after identifying suspicious activity through its monitoring of potential semiconductor diversion, according to a join statement issued with the Justice Department. In May 2025, Commerce Department investigators requested records from Nvidia regarding direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list the following month, according to the statement. U.S. authorities, working with Singaporean law enforcement officials, also conducted an on-site end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed its then-CEO Alice Huang. The Justice Department subsequently took the lead in the criminal investigation into the company. Commerce also added an Alibaba subsidiary in Singapore, Apex Enterprise Solutions, to a trade blacklist, Reuters reported. Alibaba said it would pursue all legal avenues to protect its rights and reputation, adding that Apex had never diverted advanced computing chips subject to U.S. export restrictions, according to Reuters. Meanwhile, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said at a news conference in Canberra, Australia, on Tuesday that investigations into Megaspeed were ongoing and that discussions with American authorities were continuing. "We do not want Singapore to be used and abused as a conduit by companies to circumvent America's export controls," Wong said.

cards.body: Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday. The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.” Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.” Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing. TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds. After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

The funding would be used to purchase Nvidia GB300 chips for Firmus' data center project in Indonesia, being developed with DayOne Data Centers. The company previously planned to launch an initial public offering to raise capital, but this fell apart with Firmus blaming market volatility. headlines.body: Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back. Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher. The reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the company reported strong third-quarter results. A petition calling for Huang's return had drawn more than 200,000 signatures, according to its organizers. The rally spread across the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%, each posting its strongest session since April 2025. Nvidia's board said it had received input from senior U.S. government officials and that its investigation into Huang's conduct would continue. Still, the board's reversal, President Donald Trump's administration's role and continued scrutiny of Nvidia's China business leave major questions for both investors and lawmakers. What would Washington do? Sen. Jack Reed, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Monday to appear before the committee to discuss the case. Reed did not lay out a specific list of questions for the two officials, but his statement cited reporting that Trump had been briefed by intelligence officials led by then-National Security Adviser Marco Rubio before intervening in support of Huang's return. Reed's call adds to mounting pressure on both Nvidia and the Trump administration to explain what they knew and when. Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., vice ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said Huang’s reinstatement could broaden congressional scrutiny rather than bring it to a close. “I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query,” Amo told CNBC, adding that lawmakers should also examine administration officials involved in decisions affecting Nvidia and chip sales to China. Amo said he expects the planned closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1 to proceed and that Congress would continue seeking answers both privately and publicly in the coming months. “He should start purchasing his plane tickets to Washington,” he said. “It is abundantly clear that this is ripe for questioning by Congress.” Why the reversal? On Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, Jones said the board had accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. Less than a week later, the board reversed course, saying Monday that it had unanimously voted to bring Huang back after discussions with him and input from senior U.S. government officials. Trump said he had spoken with board members and that his administration provided assurances based on the information available to it. But the board has not publicly detailed what it was told. Reed has called on Huang to disclose his communications with Trump and on Nvidia to release a transcript

headlines.body: Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO. The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the company's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers said. "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a China hawk who is retiring from Congress, told CNBC in a phone interview. "To me it's a failure of character." President Donald Trump told CNBC in an extended interview later Monday morning that he personally intervened to convince Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, saying, "I made the deal." Bacon, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation, said he wants the next Congress to conduct thorough oversight, while questioning the Trump administration's motives. "Somebody's responsible for this, and it may be" Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department is responsible for setting U.S. export controls on AI chips, Bacon said. "But I think we should get to the bottom of this." Huang, who is scheduled to testify before multiple committees on Capitol Hill starting Dec. 1, is "going to get high scrutiny in a bipartisan way when he comes next week," Bacon said. Huang's closed-door appearance before a trio of House committees is on the schedule, as the panels seek answers on the national security implications of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, MS NOW reported. The Senate banking committee announced after Huang's reinstatement that he will appear for a public hearing Dec. 3. John Fisher of Trident, a spokesman for Huang, declined to comment on the Nvidia CEO's scheduled appearances. "He better be there," Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told CNBC about Huang's scheduled Dec. 1 appearance. His reinstatement will only intensify congressional probes into Nvidia and its government connections, Amo predicted. headlines.body: Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang by a unanimous vote from its board of directors, the company announced Monday. "Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board," a statement reads. "The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." Shares of the company surged more than 30% ahead of the Nasdaq's open, erasing all of the losses incurred during Huang's leave of absence. In a Truth Social post , President Donald Trump said Nvidia "has made the correct and proper decision" in reinstating Huang, stating the USA needs his leadership and Nvidia to ensure "the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy." He further stated that the U.S. Attorney General has no evidence Huang engaged "in any unlawful conduct." The board said that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk, and part of this reassurance seems to have come from a senior level of the United States government. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board, stated. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer." Huang said he was "honored" to return to Nvidia, but took the responsibility "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment." Huang remains under investigation following reports he was entangled in an extramarital affair with a Chinese intelligence asset , with the board stating the investigation will proceed to conclusion. Reports emerged some weeks ago that Jensen Huang was having an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, a company under criminal investigation for the export of illicit AI GPUs into China. Meanwhile, a second affair with VP of health care Kimberly Powell was brought to light, prompting Huang's resignation. Nvidia has also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors "to oversee trade compliance and national security risks." The committee will continue its work, and the company is also hiring a Chief Compliance Officer "to oversee compliance across Nvidia and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee."

headlines.body: 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)의 경영 복귀에 따른 주가 급등으로 최대 1500만달러(약 221억원)의 주식 평가이익을 얻었을 수 있다는 분석이 나왔다. 트럼프 대통령이 황 CEO 복귀에 직접 관여했다고 밝히면서 이해충돌 논란이 제기됐다. 영국 파이낸셜타임스(FT)는 23일(현지시간) 미국 정부윤리청(OGE) 재산공개 자료를 분석한 결과, 트럼프 대통령이 지난 9월 30일 기준 엔비디아 주식을 최대 37만주 보유했을 것으로 추산했다. 여기에 이날 주가 상승분을 적용하면 평가이익은 최대 1500만달러에 이른다. 이는 신고된 거래금액 범위 안에서 주식을 최대한 많이 사고, 최소한으로 팔았다고 가정한 결과다. 미국 공직자 재산신고는 정확한 주식 거래금액 대신 일정 금액 구간을 기재하는 방식이어서 실제 보유량과 차이가 있을 수 있다. 반대로 매수 규모를 최소로, 매도 규모를 최대로 적용하면 추정 보유량은 3만2000주다. 이 경우 평가이익은 약 130만달러(약 19억원)로 줄어든다. FT는 10~11월 거래 내역이 공개되지 않아 실제 보유 주식 수는 확인할 수 없다고 설명했다. 이날 엔비디아 주가는 황 CEO의 경영 복귀 소식에 31.5% 급등했다. 트럼프 대통령은 복귀 결정 과정에서 자신이 핵심 역할을 했다고 밝혔다. 트럼프 대통령은 CNBC 인터뷰에서 “내가 그들을 설득했고 일을 성사시켰다”며 “이사회와 직·간접적으로 대화해왔고, 이 문제에 매우 강한 의지를 갖고 있었다”고 말했다. 황 CEO 복귀 발표 직후에는 트루스소셜에 “올바르고 타당한 결정”이라며 “엔비디아뿐 아니라 미국 경제의 번영과 성공을 위해 젠슨의 리더십이 필요하다”고 적었다. 엔비디아 이사회도 황 CEO 복귀와 관련해 미국 정부 고위급 인사들의 의견을 전달받았다고 밝혔다. 이사회는 “그런 의견을 바탕으로 황의 복귀가 국가안보상 위험을 초래하지 않는다고 확신한다”고 설명했다. 쟁점은 트럼프 대통령이 엔비디아 주식을 보유한 것으로 신고한 상황에서 주가 상승을 촉발한 경영진 인사에 관여했다는 점이다. 다만 추정 평가이익은 실제 보유량에 따라 달라지며, 주식 매도로 확정한 실현이익과도 구분된다. 민주당 소속 루벤 가예고 상원의원은 소셜미디어를 통해 “이번 발표 이전에 어떤 주식 거래 포지션을 취했는지 조사해야 한다”며 트럼프 행정부를 비판했다. 권동준 기자 djkwon@etnews.com - 권동준 기자기사 더보기 - ET Events
